body: What I Cover My focus spans the global energy landscape and the technologies reshaping it, specifically focusing on oil and gas, renewables, and tech-driven market… Copper slid to its lowest in almost four months on Friday and was heading for a fifth straight weekly loss , with traders blaming Nvidia’s (Nasdaq: NVDA) loss of Jensen Huang for the latest leg down. The exit is a convenient culprit, but the slide started before it. Copper has dropped every week since mid-October, and Goldman Sachs called the correction a matter of positioning in AI-linked stocks, not a sign that fundamentals have loosened. Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was down 0.5% at $13,519 a metric ton as of 1000 GMT, after touching $13,456, its weakest since July 17. As the Nvidia news broke on Thursday, Panmure Liberum analyst Tom Price put it bluntly: “Every time AI takes a hit, copper demand and prices come under pressure too.” He also pointed to stubborn US inflation and the prospect of Federal Reserve rate hikes. Nvidia said Huang resigned Thursday as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is interim CEO while keeping her finance job, and Harvey Jones becomes the board’s first chair. Shares closed 4.3% lower Thursday and fell about 2% more on Friday . Bloomberg reported that results are due Nov. 17, with Kress promising an all-hands meeting the next day. Huang has also agreed to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said, adding that “he has some very serious questions to answer.” The route from a boardroom crisis to the copper market runs through financing. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri said Nvidia has become a key source of funds for neoclouds and AI developers, and expects a pause in its appetite for those deals even if a new CEO holds the same course. JPMorgan analysts said they do not assume existing commitments change, but new deals could take longer or cost more. Goldman said copper positioning could stay subdued if equity markets start pricing an earlier slowdown in AI spending, even while data center construction continues. The gap matters because much of the money is not going into buildings. Mining.com’s Frédéric Tomesco and Colin McClelland flagged the builders’ budgets on Thursday. Microsoft CFO Amy Hood told investors Oct. 28 that calendar-year capital spending would reach about $170 billion , and about three-quarters of its latest quarterly spending went to short-lived assets such as chips. Alphabet held its 2026 forecast at $195 billion to $205 billion. S&P Global sees copper demand reaching 42 million metric tons by 2040, up 50%, with AI and defense each roughly tripling and adding about 4 million tons between them. Developers are also building their own power. Oilprice.com contributors Leonard Hyman and William Tilles wrote this week that published estimates point to 30 to 50 gigawatts of on-site generation at data centers within five years, mostly gas turbines. Physical buyers in China are not behaving like a market braced for weaker demand. The Yangshan copper premium, a gauge of China’s appetite for imports, hit a record $285 a ton on Friday, and copper stocks in Shanghai Futures Exchange warehouses fell 18.3% this week to 27,642 tons, the lowest since Dec. 23, Reuters reported. The gold-silver ratio is currently 79.9 — one ounce of gold is worth the same as 79.9 ounces of silver. The gold-silver ratio is the oldest relative-value measure in precious metals: it simply divides the gold price by the silver price. For most of monetary history the ratio was fixed near 15:1; in the modern free-market era it has ranged widely — from below 20 to above 100 — moving as the two metals respond differently to industrial cycles and investment flows. Traders watch the ratio as a gauge of how the two metals are priced relative to each other and to their own history. A rising ratio means gold is outperforming silver; a falling ratio means silver is gaining ground. The ratio above is calculated live from the same spot quotes shown on this page and on our gold price page . The spot price is the market price for one troy ounce of silver for immediate delivery, quoted in U.S. dollars. It is derived from the most actively traded silver futures contract together with over-the-counter dealing, and it moves nearly around the clock as trading follows the sun from New York to London, Zurich, Shanghai and Hong Kong. A troy ounce is 31.1034768 grams — about 10% heavier than the avoirdupois ounce used for groceries. Physical silver products trade at a premium above spot that covers fabrication and distribution — and because silver is far less valuable per gram than gold, the premium is proportionally larger: minting a one-ounce silver coin costs nearly as much as minting a gold one, but represents a much bigger share of the metal’s value. The spot price is for silver delivered now; a futures price is for silver delivered on a set date in the future, traded on exchanges such as COMEX. The two normally differ by the cost of carrying silver to that date — storage, insurance and interest — which is why futures usually trade slightly above spot ( contango ). When futures trade below spot ( backwardation ), it signals unusually strong demand for immediate physical delivery. The price on this page is the spot price; quotes for "silver futures" refer to the most active COMEX contract. Monetary forces: rates, the dollar, and gold. Silver is a monetary metal, and its biggest day-to-day drivers are the same ones that move all precious metals: real interest rates, the U.S. dollar, and investor demand for hard assets. This keeps silver strongly correlated with gold — but silver's market is a fraction of gold's size, so the same flows move it further, and silver routinely outpaces gold's moves in percentage terms, in both directions. title: Bitcoin Price Prediction: Where Could Bitcoin Be by Year-End? - 24/7 Wall St.
body: This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them. Bitcoin price predictions for the rest of the year vary widely, with estimates ranging from $40,000 to $80,000. Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) is trading at $65,906, down 24.7% from the start of the year and 48% below its all-time high of $126,080 in October 2025. To reach the top end of the forecast range by December 31, Bitcoin would need to rally 21%. Sellers have dominated the market for weeks. Bitcoin reached $84,082 on October 21 and has dropped 20.4% over the past 30 days, including a 4.3% decline in the last 24 hours. Research firm Bespoke noted that Bitcoin is “deep into oversold territory,” suggesting that selling pressure might soon ease. So where might Bitcoin stand at year-end? Bitcoin’s market cap is about $1.33 trillion, with roughly 20.1 million coins in circulation and a maximum supply of 21 million. As new coins are mined, the same price now represents a larger total market value than in previous cycles. If Bitcoin reaches $80,000, its market cap would be about $1.61 trillion, and returning to its all-time high would push it to around $2.54 trillion. Investor sentiment has also shifted, with money moving out of Bitcoin funds. According to SoSoValue, spot Bitcoin ETFs —funds that directly hold Bitcoin—have $89.6 billion in assets but saw net outflows of $2.14 billion over the past 30 days. All of these forecasts were made before the latest market downturn. Geoffrey Kendrick, then Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets research, stated on June 12 that Bitcoin had already hit its bottom at $59,000. However, Bitcoin closed at $58,566 on June 30, just under that call and 11% below it, marking its lowest close in the past year. Galaxy Research took the opposite view on the same day. Its cycle study, which looked at where analysts say Bitcoin bottoms , expected a fourth-quarter bottom between $40,000 and $46,000, 30% to 39% below Bitcoin’s price. In a softer outlook, the firm suggested a low between $51,000 and $54,000. On the upside, the $80,000 mark remains a recurring target. A market observer urged caution around that level on September 18, emphasizing the need for positive ETF flows. A Bitcoin price prediction for November suggested that if Bitcoin held above $76,141, it could trade between $76,000 and $82,000, but Bitcoin has since fallen below $76,141. The likelihood of Bitcoin hitting $80,000 by December 31 appears low, with the most probable year-end price between $65,000 and $73,000. The Federal Reserve, which raised the top of its target range to 4% on September 16, is scheduled to meet again on December 9, and fed funds futures, contracts that track rate expectations, place an 89% probability on another quarter-point hike. Since reaching $86,597 on September 21, Bitcoin’s price has trended downward. A key level to monitor is $58,566. A close below it after the Fed’s December 9 decision could make the low scenario more likely, while a Fed pause and a rise above $73,043 might revive the high scenario. Over a longer horizon, Bitcoin is up 72.5% over the past three years, and a look at how much one Bitcoin could be worth in 2030 takes that longer view. So, what could happen if Bitcoin falls below $65,000, and who might be affected by this decline? Bitcoin’s price chart highlights three support levels, each of which held earlier this summer when buyers returned to the market. Miners will likely feel the impact of any price drop first since they often sell newly mined coins to cover their operating expenses. The mining difficulty, the measure of how hard it is to earn new Bitcoin, adjusts roughly every two weeks. According to Mempool. a significant decrease of about 5.5% is expected at the next adjustment. Such a decline typically indicates miners have started shutting down operations, and as Bitcoin approaches $62,844, more miners may sell reserves to stay afloat. Strategy Inc. holds 850,364 Bitcoin, as reported in its November 9 filing, at an average price of $75,456 per coin. That means, at current trading prices, its holdings are worth about $56 billion against an initial investment of approximately $64.2 billion, putting the firm at a loss . While Strategy can withstand these paper losses, the greater concern arises from its substantial debt, around $6.7 billion in convertible debt and $13.3 billion in preferred stock, which is not fully covered by its $5.07 billion in cash assets that can only sustain dividends and interest for 3.4 years. CEO Phong Le noted in October that Bitcoin could drop by as much as 78%, down to $18,000, before the company’s Bitcoin would only just cover its liabilities. The stock shows signs of stress, having closed at $112 on November 13, reflecting a 46.5% decline over the year. Furthermore, MSCI plans to remove Strategy from its global indexes by the end of November. Ongoing selling in spot Bitcoin ETFs, funds that hold actual Bitcoin for shareholders, such as the Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust ( NYSEARCA: BTC ), adds to the pressure. These funds recorded net outflows in every session from November 5 to November 13, with their total net assets sliding from $109.3 billion on October 21 to $86.2 billion. When investors cash out, these funds must sell Bitcoin, increasing supply just as the price tests $65,000. Geoffrey Kendrick, Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets research, said on June 12 that Bitcoin had bottomed at $59,000. Bitcoin did dip just below that level in late June before rebounding in August. Meanwhile, Alex Thorn of Galaxy Research anticipates Bitcoin could sink to a range between $40,000 and $46,000 in the fourth quarter, a 30% to 39% drop from current levels. In a more optimistic scenario, the low could settle around $51,000 to $54,000. body: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins supported gradual interest rate increases on November 14, 2026 , citing persistent inflation and economic uncertainty. Her remarks, reported by Reuters, come as U.S. agriculture faces rising debt, elevated production costs and tighter operating margins. With the USDA projecting $605.1 billion in total farm debt for 2026 , additional monetary tightening could increase financing expenses just as producers prepare their 2027 planting budgets and investment decisions. The Federal Reserve's benchmark interest rate currently stands at 3.75% to 4% , with markets anticipating another quarter-point increase at the December 8-9 meeting. Collins favors smaller, measured adjustments rather than aggressive tightening, although she acknowledged that economic data could change the policy outlook. For farmers, higher rates can translate into more expensive operating loans, machinery financing and farmland purchases, particularly for operations relying on variable-rate credit.

title: Can AI Infrastructure Demand Sustain NVIDIA's Q3 Data Center Growth? - Yahoo Finance
body: NVIDIA Corporation NVDA is scheduled to report third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings on Nov. 17, and expectations are high. The company continues to dominate the artificial intelligence (AI) computing market and remains one of the biggest beneficiaries of rising AI infrastructure spending. NVIDIA's powerful graphics processing units (GPUs), networking products and full-stack AI platforms have become essential for companies building and operating AI data centers. With hyperscale cloud providers, AI startups, enterprises and governments increasing their investments in AI infrastructure, NVIDIA appears well-positioned to deliver another strong quarter. The company's third-quarter revenue guidance of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, reflects this strong demand. NVIDIA Corporation price-eps-surprise | NVIDIA Corporation Quote NVIDIA's Data Center business has been the biggest contributor to its recent growth. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Data Center revenues jumped 117% year over year and 18% sequentially to a record $89.02 billion. The growth was driven by strong demand for its Blackwell Ultra infrastructure, with both hyperscale and AI Clouds, Industrial and Enterprise (ACIE) customers contributing significantly. This positive trend is expected to have continued in the third quarter. One of the biggest growth drivers could be continued investments by hyperscale cloud providers. During the last earnings call, NVIDIA's management noted that the cloud industry's backlog exceeded $2 trillion, while capital expenditures by the top five hyperscalers are expected to reach nearly $800 billion in 2026 and $1.3 trillion in 2027. Amazon Web Services has also announced plans to deploy an additional 2 million NVIDIA GPUs between the third quarter of fiscal 2027 and the second quarter of fiscal 2029. These investments should have supported demand for NVIDIA's computing platforms in the third quarter. Another important growth driver is the rising demand from AI startups, enterprises, sovereign customers and regional cloud providers. In the second quarter, ACIE revenues surged 138% year over year and 25% sequentially to $40.31 billion. Growth was driven by additional capacity from NeoCloud providers, rising enterprise and AI startup demand, and hyperscalers purchasing AI cloud capacity to supplement their own infrastructure. This diversified customer base is anticipated to have supported Data Center growth in the third quarter. The ramp-up of NVIDIA's latest products is likely to have provided another boost. The company has commenced production shipments of its next-generation Vera Rubin platform and expects it to account for approximately 20% of Data Center revenues in the third quarter. Its full-stack AI infrastructure, including GPUs, CPUs, networking products and software, also helps customers build and operate AI data centers more efficiently. Growing adoption of agentic AI, which requires substantial computing power to perform complex tasks, could further increase demand for NVIDIA's products. However, supply constraints and rising memory prices remain important concerns. NVIDIA expects its third-quarter gross margin to be approximately 74%, reflecting higher component costs. Moreover, management expects sequential growth to be driven primarily by ACIE, while hyperscale growth is expected to accelerate in the fourth quarter. Overall, strong AI infrastructure spending, expanding customer demand and the Vera Rubin ramp-up are likely to have contributed to NVIDIA's Data Center business growth in the third quarter. title: Nvidia Stock Is Still a Buy After CEO Jensen Huang’s Departure - Barron's
Euro zone inflation hits 4% for first time in three years as interest rate hike looms
summary: It was driven by energy inflation, which surged above 20% in October.
body: Inflation in the euro area jumped to a three-year high of 4% in October, a flash estimate showed on Wednesday. The reading is in line with the expectations of economists polled by Reuters and was up from 3.8% in September . Officials said the increase was largely due to surging energy costs, with energy inflation rising to 20.8% from 18.9% in September. Europe, a net energy importer, is vulnerable to external energy shocks and has seen prices rise steadily since the start of the Iran war. October marked the first time inflation in the euro zone has hit or exceeded the 4% threshold since Sept. 2023's reading of 4.3%. Inflation also varied across the 21 euro zone economies, with Lithuania recording the hottest inflation rate of 6.1% while Malta's was the lowest at 2.3%. All euro zone countries saw inflation hold above the European Central Bank's 2% target. The euro was up 0.6% against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday morning, although the greenback fell against a basket of major currencies as counting continued in the U.S. midterm elections, while the yield on the 10-year German bund — broadly seen as a benchmark for euro zone bonds — was marginally higher. Policymakers said underlying inflation and wages were broadly stable, despite inflation sitting at a three-year high. The European Central Bank kept its key interest rate at 2.5% last month, following a hike of 25 basis points in September. Shortly before Wednesday's inflation print, markets were pricing in a 71.8% chance of a hike at the ECB's final meeting of the year in December. Following the data release, markets were pricing in more than a 72% chance of rates rising. Robert Mertens, global capital markets senior analyst at Validus Risk Management, cautioned that "ongoing turmoil in the French bond market is placing constraints on ECB policy" and the bank's capacity to get inflation under control. "Should we see an easing in French political unrest, the ECB could potentially pursue a more aggressive hiking path," he said. "If the ECB can deploy more aggressive tightening relative to the Federal Reserve, we would see increased Euro support and upside versus the Dollar."

title: Gold Slips as Rising Real Yields Outweigh Cooler October CPI - FXEmpire
body: Gold kicks off the Friday session with fresh U.S. inflation data and a sharp rise in Treasury real yields. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday that the October CPI rose 0.4% month-over-month on a seasonally adjusted basis, down from 0.6% in September. Core CPI, excluding food and energy, advanced 0.3%, matching August and September. Energy prices rose 0.7% during October after a 5.2% increase during the month of September, while gasoline increased 1% on a seasonally adjusted basis. For gold, the combination is not necessarily bullish. Despite the fact that the report showed some easing in headline monthly inflation, it wasnât like it had a broad retreat in core prices. Slower headline inflation can reduce inflation-hedge demand and support expectations of a less restrictive Federal Reserve, yet the steady 0.3% core pace may keep policymakers cautious. The immediate driver of the market is going to be the change in expected rates and real yields rather than the CPI release itself. The Treasuryâs latest published daily par real yield curve is through yesterday. The 5-year real yield rose to 2.64%, the 10-year to 2.86%, and the 30-year to 3.25% on November 12. These figures were up from 2.35%, 2.63%, and 3.07%, respectively, on November 6. Higher real yields continue to cause problems as they increase the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. The yield curve has also steepened in real terms over the long end, with a 30-year rate above the 5-year. These Treasury figures are derived from TIPS par yields, not actual security prices. They do not establish a mechanically inverse relationship with gold by themselves, but a broad rise in inflation-adjusted yields is a meaningful hurdle. The CPI report itself carries data limitations. BLS did not collect October 2025 survey data during the lapse in appropriations via Congress, so it cannot publish a 12-month percentage change for October 2026 for the affected series. Goldâs next test will be whether or not real yields stabilize after the post-CPI increase and whether investors interpret the report as easing inflation pressure or persisting core strength. It appears that the persisting core strength scenario is the one that is winning out, and therefore itâs worth watching that very closely. title: Silver Price Forecast: Why has XAG/USD climbed to near $50.50 despite Fed rate hike bets? - www.tmgm.com
body: Rising Treasury yields could limit gains in Silver (XAG/USD), as expectations build for a more aggressive Federal Reserve (Fed) policy stance. The metal is nevertheless recovering from the previous day’s modest decline, trading near $50.50 per troy ounce in Friday’s Asian session. To assess long-term yield dynamics and the forces driving this year’s movements, Rabobank analysts have broken down the 10-year US Treasury yield. They describe their latest US rates research as “a detailed decomposition of the 10yr UST yield and how it has changed in 2026,” providing a framework for that assessment. Bets on a December Fed rate increase have strengthened following this week’s higher-than-expected US Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation figures. According to the CME FedWatch tool, traders now assign nearly 85.5% odds to a rate hike at the central bank’s next meeting on 8-9 December, with a 14.5% probability of a half-point increase. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 50-basis-point hike should be considered if core inflation stays elevated. Friday’s US Producer Price Index (PPI) release will be the next focus for indications of inflation pressures and the Fed’s interest rate decision. Forecasts point to a 6.6% YoY increase in headline PPI for October, alongside a 5.0% YoY rise in core PPI for the same reporting period. Separately, CNBC reported that US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that the US should stop pursuing an agreement with Iran. In a Truth Social post, Trump wrote: “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed,” Investors trade Silver extensively, and the precious metal has long served both as a store of value and as a medium of exchange. While Gold attracts greater interest, traders may choose Silver for its intrinsic value, to diversify their portfolios or as a possible hedge when inflation is high. Exposure can be gained by purchasing physical Silver coins or bars, or through instruments such as Exchange Traded Funds that follow its price in international markets. A broad set of influences can drive Silver prices. When geopolitical tensions rise or concerns about a severe recession grow, its safe-haven appeal can lift prices, though the effect is generally smaller than for Gold. Lower interest rates also tend to support Silver because it generates no yield. Since the metal is quoted in US dollars (XAG/USD), movements in the US Dollar (USD) matter: dollar strength generally restrains Silver prices, while a weaker dollar is likely to push them higher. Investment demand, recycling rates and supply from mining can influence prices too; Silver is far more abundant than Gold. With electrical conductivity among the highest of all metals, exceeding that of Copper and Gold, Silver has extensive industrial applications, notably in electronics and solar energy. Prices can rise when demand surges and tend to fall when it weakens. Developments in the US, Chinese and Indian economies can also drive price fluctuations. Large industrial sectors in the US and, especially, China consume Silver across a range of processes. In India, consumer demand for Silver jewellery is another important factor in determining prices. Given their comparable safe-haven status, a rise in Gold prices is usually accompanied by gains in Silver, whose price tends to track Gold’s movements. Investors may use the Gold/Silver ratio to assess the metals’ relative valuations. This ratio measures how many ounces of Silver equal the value of one ounce of Gold. A high reading may be interpreted by some investors as a sign that Silver is undervalued or Gold is overvalued. A low reading, by contrast, could indicate that Gold is undervalued compared with Silver. body: Selling pressure remains firmly in control of Bitcoin (BTC), which has deepened its correction by more than 8% to touch an intraday low of $67,568 on Friday. Oversold technical readings have failed to ease the pressure. Continued outflows from Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), liquidation of leveraged positions and reduced risk appetite are clouding the outlook for the Crypto King. Further undermining sentiment are the steep fall in Nvidia (NVDA) shares and news this week of CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, both of which have reinforced the broader shift away from risk. A controversy involving CEO Jensen Huang’s personal relationships, followed by his resignation on Thursday, has sent Nvidia shares down more than 13% so far this week. Nvidia has consequently lost its standing as the world’s most valuable publicly traded company. The sell-off has also prompted a broader retreat from risk, putting pressure on assets such as cryptocurrencies. Against this backdrop, Bitcoin’s correction exceeded 8%, taking it to a low of $67,568 on Friday, a level last seen in mid-August. Liquidations swept across the cryptocurrency market as prices moved lower this week. According to the Coinglass chart below, BTC positions worth more than $1.2 billion were liquidated, predominantly longs. This underscores the bullish positioning of leveraged Bitcoin traders. Nvidia’s weakness and developments surrounding CEO Jensen Huang have increased selling pressure on Bitcoin, but they were not the main reasons for its fall, Bitunix Analyst Dean Chen told FXStreet in an exclusive interview. In his assessment, Bitcoin was already weakening before Nvidia’s latest pullback, indicating that factors specific to cryptocurrencies had a greater influence. “I think blaming Bitcoin’s decline on Nvidia is a little too convenient. The timeline doesn’t really support that explanation,” Chen said. He pointed out that Bitcoin reached its peak near $87,300 on September 21, whereas Nvidia’s high came later, on October 6. Rather than setting off the initial decline, the correction in AI stocks and news involving Jensen Huang heightened anxiety in a market that was already fragile, he added. Chen concluded: “I’m not saying Bitcoin can’t bounce from here. It certainly can, especially if forced selling eases and short positions begin to close. But I wouldn’t confuse a relief rally with a real recovery,” Bitcoin has seen softer institutional demand this week, with SoSoValue data pointing to a third consecutive week of net outflows from BTC spot ETFs. Net withdrawals had reached $595.98 million by Wednesday, following last week’s net outflows of $1.28 billion. A continuation and acceleration of withdrawals through Friday could increase the pressure on BTC and deepen its price correction. Corporate support, which has traditionally cushioned Bitcoin during steep corrections, has suffered another setback this week. Global index provider MSCI confirmed on Wednesday that Strategy would be excluded from its global indices, the MSCI USA Index and the MSCI World Index. The exclusion list also includes Tokyo-listed Metaplanet, another company that buys and holds BTC. Effective December 1, the companies will be removed from the MSCI Japan Small Cap Index. To align their portfolios with these changes, index funds following the affected benchmarks may have to sell shares in Strategy and Metaplanet by November 30 and December 1. The direct impact of MSCI’s decision is on the two companies’ shares, not their Bitcoin holdings. Nevertheless, the effects could spill over into the cryptocurrency, given the substantial role of Bitcoin in their treasury holdings. Strategy remains the largest corporate Bitcoin holder with 850,364 BTC, while Metaplanet Inc. ranks second with 44,000 BTC. title: Goldman Sachs Forecasts Copper Prices to Reach $15,600 per Tonne by December 2027 - Yahoo Finance
body: Goldman Sachs expects copper prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) to reach $15,600 per tonne by December 2027, representing an increase of approximately 13% from current spot levels. The investment bank's forecast follows a period of rising copper prices, with the metal trading at just under $10,000 per tonne during the previous year. Goldman Sachs attributed its outlook to increasing demand from electrification, energy security initiatives, strategic inventory accumulation, data centre development and infrastructure supporting artificial intelligence. The bank also identified constraints on mine production as a factor influencing the outlook for copper supply. According to Goldman Sachs, policies introduced by the United States and China over the past year to secure domestic supply chains have increased competition between the two countries for refined copper. Both countries have sought to improve access to the metal, which is used in electrical infrastructure, industrial equipment and technologies associated with energy systems. The bank indicated that competition for refined copper has contributed to a reduction in inventories held outside the United States, bringing stocks to seasonal lows. Goldman Sachs said these developments have added upward pressure to copper prices alongside existing structural limitations on mine supply. Goldman Sachs identified electrification and investment in data centres as important contributors to its projected increase in copper demand. The bank also cited artificial intelligence infrastructure and energy security programmes as sources of additional consumption. Alongside industrial demand, inventory accumulation linked to supply security objectives has contributed to competition for available refined copper. Goldman Sachs expects these demand factors, combined with limitations on mine production and reduced inventories outside the United States, to support its forecast of $15,600 per tonne by December 2027. The projection represents the bank's assessment of future market conditions rather than a guaranteed price outcome.

body: [Digital Today reporter Oh Sang-yeop] South Korea's stock market this week is expected to look for a rebound direction while checking Nvidia's results, the first to be released after Jensen Huang resigned. Signs of bargain buying and recovering foreign inflows have emerged recently, but doubts remain over the profitability of artificial intelligence (AI) investment and U.S. long-term interest rates. How much Nvidia eases those concerns will be key. The KOSPI closed on Nov. 13 down 52.20 points, or 0.98 percent, at 5,290.53 from the previous session. It rose as high as 5,504.44 in early trade, but gave up all gains as foreign investors turned net sellers. The KOSDAQ ended 0.45 percent higher at 699.66. The latest U.S. stock market session was also mixed on weakness in technology shares. On Nov. 13 (local time), the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed up 0.1 percent at 52,347.55, but the S&P 500 fell 0.4 percent to 7,561.67 and the Nasdaq dropped 0.9 percent to 25,136.27. On a weekly basis, all three indexes rose. Korean stocks have tried to rebound after sliding to the 5,000 level recently, but direction remains unclear. Corporate earnings outlooks are relatively solid, but financing burdens for AI companies, rising U.S. long-term rates and unstable foreign flows are alternately shaking the index. The most important event this week is Nvidia's third-quarter earnings release on Nov. 17 (local time). Nvidia will release fiscal 2027 third-quarter results after the close and hold a conference call the same day. The market is expected to focus more on data centre revenue, forward guidance and the sustainability of AI investment than on revenue and operating profit alone. Recent doubts about the AI industry are also focused less on insufficient demand than on whether massive capital spending can translate into actual cash flow and profits. Uncertainty has grown further, in particular, after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (젠슨 황) resigned on Nov. 12. Nvidia's board appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, and the company said there would be no disruptions to customers and its product roadmap. If Nvidia's results beat market expectations and demand for AI accelerators and data centres is reaffirmed as solid, investor sentiment in semiconductor and AI-related shares, which have fallen sharply, could revive. If guidance falls short of expectations, volatility could spread to Korean semiconductor shares as concerns over a management change overlap with worries about investment profitability. Still, some assessments say it is hard to view domestic semiconductor earnings themselves as having been significantly damaged. Profit forecasts for Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix remain high, and semiconductor exports in early November are also maintaining a solid trend. The recent stock-price decline is seen as having been driven more by rates, flows and worsening sentiment toward the AI industry than by earnings. The industry, accordingly, sees a need to maintain the existing strategy centred on heavyweight semiconductor shares while also checking whether foreign inflows recover. Foreign investors have turned net buyers on some sessions recently, but they switched back to net selling on Nov. 13, making it too early to judge it as a trend-like return. Interest rates are also a key variable. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield rose as high as 5.17 percent intraday on Nov. 13, the highest level since October. The U.S. producer price index (PPI) rose 0.3 percent from the previous month, below an expected 0.4 percent, but the year-on-year increase reached 6.5 percent, showing inflation burdens remain. High rates raise funding costs for businesses requiring large amounts of capital such as AI data centres. That means even if Nvidia's results are strong, if long-term yields keep rising, the pace of valuation recovery in growth shares could be limited.
